Título: The European Commission adopts the European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS)
Conteúdo Detalhado: The European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS) were approved by the Commission today for use by all businesses governed by the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD). This is a step in the right direction toward a sustainable EU economy. The complete spectrum of environmental, social, and governance issues are covered by the standards, including those relating to climate change, biodiversity, and human rights. Investors can use the information they provide to better understand the sustainability impact of the businesses they invest in. In order to achieve a very high level of interoperability between EU and global standards and to prevent enterprises from reporting information twice, they also take into account negotiations with the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) and the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI). For various companies, the reporting requirements will gradually be implemented.

Título: ISSB publishes the first global sustainability disclosure standards
Conteúdo Detalhado: The International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) announced its first standards today, IFRS S1 and IFRS S2, ushering in a new era of sustainability-related reporting in global capital markets. The Standards will help to increase trust and confidence in corporate sustainability disclosures in order to guide investment decisions. For the first time, the Standards establish a consistent vocabulary for communicating the impact of climate-related risks and opportunities on a company's prospects. ISSB Chair Emmanuel Faber will officially launch the Standards at the IFRS Foundation's annual conference, as well as through events hosted by stock exchanges around the world, including those in Frankfurt, Johannesburg, Lagos, London, New York, and Santiago de Chile; the ASEAN Capital Markets Forum will also host a launch event in Singapore. About the Standards : IFRS S1 establishes a series of disclosure standards to enable businesses to communicate with investors about the sustainability-related risks and opportunities they face in the short, medium, and long term. IFRS S2 specifies particular climate-related disclosures and is intended to be used in conjunction with IFRS S1. Both completely integrate the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD) guidelines.

Título: "Fit for 55": European Council passes significant pieces of legislation that will advance the 2030 climate goals
Conteúdo Detalhado: Five laws were approved by the Council today that will allow the EU to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in the major economic sectors while ensuring that the most vulnerable citizens, microbusinesses, and sectors that are vulnerable to carbon leakage are effectively supported in the climate transition. The legislation are a part of the 'Fit for 55' package, which aligns EU policies with its promise to reduce net greenhouse gas emissions by at least 55% by 2030 compared to 1990 levels and to attain climate neutrality by 2050. The final step of the decision-making process is the Council vote.  EU Emissions trading system The new regulations raise the overall target for emissions reductions in the EU ETS sectors from 2005 levels to 62% by 2030. Maritime transport emissions For the first time, shipping-related emissions will be covered by the EU ETS. There will be a gradual introduction of requirements for shipping corporations to surrender allowances: 40% for certified emissions starting in 2024, 70% in 2025, and 100% in 2026. Buildings, road transportation, and other industries To assure cost-effective emissions reductions in these sectors, which have so far proven challenging to decarbonize, a new, independent emissions trading system has been formed for buildings, road transport, and additional sectors (mostly small industry). Distributors who distribute fuel to buildings, roads, and other sectors will be subject to the new system starting in 2027. Aviation-related emissions Free emission allowances for the aviation industry will be phased out gradually, and full auctioning will begin in 2026. 20 million permits will be set aside until December 31, 2030, to encourage aeroplane operators to switch to alternative fuels. Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism A method called the Carbon Border Adjustment method (CBAM) is focused on importing goods from carbon-intensive sectors. The goal of CBAM is to prevent, in full compliance with international trade regulations, that the EU's efforts to reduce greenhouse gas emissions are undermined by rising emissions outside of its borders as a result of shifting production to nations with less aggressive climate change policies or increasing imports of carbon-intensive goods. The Social Climate Fund In order to help vulnerable households, microbusinesses, and transport users deal with the economic consequences of an emissions trading system for buildings, road transport, and other sectors, member states will use the Social Climate Fund to finance initiatives and projects.

Título: A new regulation has been established on foreign branch campuses in Hainan
Conteúdo Detalhado: The Interim Regulation on the Establishment of Institutes by Overseas Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) in the Hainan Free Trade Port (HFTP) ("the Regulation") was jointly issued by the Ministry of Education (MOE) and the Hainan Provincial Government to encourage wider, deeper, and more flexible cooperation in international education. The Regulation outlines in a methodical manner the fundamental rules governing the construction of institutions or campuses by foreign higher education providers in the HFTP, based on the Law on HFTP and the Master Plan for the Development of HFTP. The Regulation demands rigorous adherence to Chinese laws and rules, with no violations of the nation's sovereignty, security, or the general welfare. The campuses are governed by regional educational administrations because they are recognised as legal entities in China. They must provide classes that introduce the Chinese Constitution, laws, moral principles, and national circumstances. Additionally, they should only plan social events or open gatherings that are permitted by pertinent national laws.

Título: Climate-related Disclosures to Become Mandatory in 2024, According to HKEX
Conteúdo Detalhado: The Exchange wants to impose additional climate-related disclosures in line with the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) Climate Standard1 and require all issuers to include information about climate change in their ESG reports. The ISSB Climate Standard outlines comprehensive climate disclosures and expands on the TCFD guidelines' core ideas. The suggestions represent a substantial step towards fulfilling the Hong Kong Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group's3 pledge to require TCFD-aligned disclosures by 2025. The Exchange proposes interim provisions4 for some disclosures (such as financial effects of climate-related risks and opportunities, scope 3 emissions, and certain cross-industry metrics) for the first two reporting years after the effective date of January 1, 2024, taking into account the issuers' readiness and their concerns.

Título: SFDR Amendments Proposed by EU Financial Regulators
Conteúdo Detalhado: The three European Supervisory Authorities (ESAs) have issued a joint consultation paper outlining proposed changes to the disclosure structure established by the Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation (SFDR). Following a mandate from the European Commission in April 2022 to review and revise SFDR's regulatory technical standards (RTSs), one of the ESAs' recommendations is to expand the existing list of principal adverse impacts' (PAIs) universal social indicators to include disclosures such as interference in trade union formation. The ESAs have also advocated improving existing indicators, methodology, and calculation formulae, as well as product disclosures relating decarbonisation targets.The paper outlines technical revisions to the SFDR Delegated Regulation, such as improvements for disclosures on how sustainable investments ‘do not significantly harm’ the environment and society.

Título: HMRC Update on the VAT and value shifting consultation
Conteúdo Detalhado: HMRC published a consultation document, "VAT and Value Shifting," in January 2021, consulting on proposed changes to the way the consideration for a bundle of separate supplies is apportioned for VAT purposes. Given concerns that the rules allowed for manipulation of the values assigned to the various elements of the bundle in order to achieve inappropriate VAT savings, the government proposed more stringent rules to prevent such manipulation.  Revenue and Customs Brief 2 (2023) has now announced that no legislative changes will be made. Instead, HMRC has concluded that the most effective way to address valuation concerns is to provide businesses with practical guidance on apportionment methods. This is through Guidelines for Compliance and improvements to other guidance.

Conteúdo Detalhado: The Securities and Exchange Commission amended its rules today to require registrants to disclose information reflecting the relationship between executive compensation paid by a registrant and financial performance. The rules carry out a requirement imposed by the Dodd-Frank Act. In 2015, the Commission proposed pay versus performance disclosure rules, and in January of this year, it reopened the comment period on the proposal. The amendments specifically demand that registrants submit a table containing information on executive compensation and financial performance metrics for their five most recent fiscal years. A registrant will be required to report its total shareholder return (TSR), the TSR of companies in its peer group, its net income, and a financial performance measure of its choice with regard to the measures of performance. Registrants will be required to explain the relationships between the executive remuneration actually paid and each of the performance metrics, as well as the relationship between the registrant's TSR and the TSR of its chosen peer group, using the information provided in the table. A registrant will also be required to provide a list of three to seven financial performance measures that it determines are its most important performance measures for linking executive compensation actually paid to company performance. Smaller reporting companies will be subject to scaled disclosure requirements under the rules.

Título: Geological Carbon Storage Policy Released by BLM for Public Lands
Conteúdo Detalhado: The Bureau of Land Management has released a new policy regarding the geologic sequestration of carbon dioxide on public lands as part of an all-encompassing plan to battle climate change and lower carbon dioxide levels in the atmosphere. The method of carefully injecting carbon dioxide, the most prevalent greenhouse gas, deep underground prevents it from ever reentering the atmosphere and aggravating the climate catastrophe. Since the 1940s, carbon dioxide has been injected underground in the United States, but usually as a temporary solution to increase oil production. This is the first time BLM has released a directive that permits the long-term storage of carbon dioxide underground. The new instruction memo offers guidance for authorising rights-of-way for site characterization, transportation, injection, capture, and permanent storage of carbon dioxide at appropriately classified injection well locations, paving the way for geologic carbon sequestration projects on BLM-managed lands. A right-of-way grant enables rights and privileges for a certain use of the land for a predetermined amount of time suitable for the project's lifespan. The instruction memo will support uniform processing of right-of-way requests for carbon sequestration projects on all BLM-managed lands and give BLM staff advice on how to handle compliance with other applicable laws, environmental review, the authorizations' term (a 30-year renewable term), rental payments, cost recovery, and sufficient monitoring and long-term stewardship.

Título: Framework under International Law : UNCLOS defines the "Area" to be the Common Heritage of Mankind
Conteúdo Detalhado: Depending on whether mining operations are conducted inside or outside of a country's borders, different rules under international law apply. Coastal waters, the continental shelf, the high seas, and "the area" are the main spatial areas that UNCLOS distinguishes between and specifies the nations' respective rights and obligations for. The territorial seas of the coastal states with exclusive sovereignty extend up to twelve nautical miles, depending on the classification under UNCLOS Article 3. (UNCLOS Articles 2 et seq.). The coastal nations have exclusive rights to exploit natural resources, both living and non-living, in the Exclusive Economic Zone (up to 200 nautical miles) and on the continental shelf (usually 200 nautical miles, or further in case of appropriate natural conditions). When exploring for or exploiting of mineral resources on the continental shelf, states are to comply with the requirements of Part XII of UNCLOS - "Protection and preservation of the marine environment". UNCLOS Articles 192 et seq. oblige coastal states to preserve and protect the marine environment. According to UNCLOS Article 194 (5), appropriate measures are necessary to protect and preserve rare or fragile ecosystems. According to UNCLOS Article 208 (3), national measures shall be no less effective than the internationally agreed level of protection. In Part XI, UNCLOS refers to the seabed beyond the national continental shelf as "The Area". UNCLOS Article 136 declares "The Area" to be the "Common Heritage of Mankind". The principle of "Common Heritage of Mankind" is usually assigned five core elements. First, UNCLOS Article 137 (1) provides, similar to the high seas, for a prohibition of appropriation of the deep seabed as a whole or any part thereof. UNCLOS Article 137 (2), also applies to mineral resources as long as they are still under the seabed surface. However, according to UNCLOS Article 137 (2), sentence 2, an appropriation of mineral resources is licit if it is done pursuant to the specifications of Part XI. Secondly, UNCLOS puts the exploitation of mineral resources of “The Area” under international administration (UNCLOS Article 137 (2), sentence 2, and UNCLOS Articles 156 and 157). The ISA, based in Kingston, Jamaica, is in charge of the administration. Third, UNCLOS Article 141 calls for “The Area” to be used exclusively for peaceful purposes. Fourth, UNCLOS Article 145 stipulates that "effective protection of the marine environment from harmful effects" is to be ensured. Fifth, UNCLOS Article 140 (2) and Articles 160 et seq. provide for financial and other economic revenues and benefits be shared equitably among all states ("benefit sharing").

Título: Germany issued ordinance on the the protection of marine areas
Conteúdo Detalhado: Germany issued six new ordinances n the protection of the marine environment in the North and Baltic Seas.The marine protected areas Doggerbank, Borkum Riffgrund, and Sylter Außenriff- stliche Deutsche Bucht in the North Sea, and Fehmarnbelt, Kadetrinne, and Pommersche Bucht - Rönnebank in the Baltic Sea, are now legally protected under national legislation. The locations are in the Exclusive Economic Zones (EEZ) of the North and Baltic Seas, making the federal government is responsible for them.The introduction of dredge waste into the sea in marine protected areas, the operation of aquacultures, and the construction of artificial islands are all prohibited under the new rules. Anyone wishing to generate energy, extract natural resources, or construct underwater cables in these areas must first demonstrate through an impact assessment that the project will not have a significant negative impact on the marine environment.

Título: U.S Fish and Wildlife Service revises policy on mitigating adverse impact of development on wildlife and its habitat
Conteúdo Detalhado: The US Fish and Wildlife Service has announced additional efforts to reduce the negative effects of land and water development on wildlife and their habitats in the United States. A modification of the Service's Mitigation Policy, which has guided agency recommendations to address these concerns since 1981, will provide a broad and flexible framework to encourage conservation while permitting economic activity to continue.It broadens the scope of mitigation to include larger-scale pressures that can wreak havoc on wildlife when combined with development, such as climate change and invasive species.
